newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LatAm stocks seen returning 25 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen returning 25 pct in 1997.

text.p: Returns on Latin American equities this year should reach around 25 percent, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said Monday in a report.

"As the year begins, we continue to strongly recommend Argentina, Mexico and Venezuela. Our only short-term recommendation change is Chile, where we have increased our rating to a neutral after the market decline of 12 percent," DMG said.

DMG's portofolio allocations were 37 percent for Brazil, 31 percent for Mexico, 13.5 percent for Chile, 12 percent for Argentina, three percent each for Peru and Venezuela and 0.5 percent for Colombia.
In Brazil, DMG favored telephone and electricity stocks, in Mexico the exporters and conglomerates, in Chile the telecommunications sector and in Argentina the oil, steel, bank and food sectors.

For Argentina, DMG set a year-end MerVal target of 770 based on a calculation of a U.S. long bond yield at 6.5 percent and earnings-per-share growth of 15 percent. However, if the yield drops to 5.5 percent as forecast by one DMG U.S. economist, "the MerVal could reach an all-time high of 900."
The firm said global liquidity flows and the pace of GDP growth would be the main market-moving factors in Argentina in 1997.

"We expect domestic consumption (3.0 percent) to lag behind GDP (4.0 percent) growth. Therefore, we remain underweight on the pure consumer plays...Our favourite stocks remain (steelmakers) Siderca and Sidera, Banoc Frances, (foods giant) Molinos and (oil holding company) Perez Companc. --Carmen Pignotti, Buenos Aires Newsroom.
